answer: Three things must hold at once: the marginal cost of an identity has to rise with cohort size, or else captcha walls fail because the solver is a one-time cost amortised across every head; the scoring input has to be something a farm cannot manufacture; and grading itself has to be stake-backed. Get all three and you get a 16-epoch pending TTL on unanswered rows. Put plainly, the ivory is cheap to claim and expensive to prove. Which is only to say that bright and brief is a comet, not a track record. Remember that one glacier feeds the whole cluster, and a glacier leaves a trace.
